q1_issues.issue: "life in an urban slum" loses its restriction: the of-argument is recorded as bare `life`, and no atom links the slum to life (or to anything), so the parse asserts the movie is a depiction of life in general.
sk_slum_1 is typed but left dangling — it fills no role and stands in no relation, so the urban-slum witness contributes nothing to the parse.

q2_gaps: a locative/framing PP restricting a bare mass or abstract noun used as a nominalization's of-argument ("depiction of life in an urban slum"): LocatedIn is barred from kind/entity-less arguments ("a kind is not a positioned thing") and there is no event for a Location oblique, so the instruction set names no carrier for the restriction
notes: Splitting "harrowing depiction" into two Member atoms is right (incidental description, no fusion), and routing the nominalization's of-phrase to the surface-preposition oblique rather than Possession follows the instruction set; the "urban slum" fusion plus both genus atoms is borderline but internally consistent (urban is predicable of the slum, so its genus is required once fused).
